p='docs/index.rst'
s=open(p).read()
anchor="    pm.hook.myhook(config=config, args=args, new_arg=\"get this\")\n"
add=anchor+'''
.. _hookimpl_arg_default:

Hookimpl argument defaults
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
A hookimpl may also declare a default value for an argument. The value a
hookimpl receives is chosen in this order:

1. the value passed by the hook call,
2. the hookspec's default value for the argument,
3. the hookimpl's own default value.

The hookimpl's default is therefore only used when neither the call nor the
hookspec provides the argument, for example when a newer hookimpl runs
against an older hookspec that does not have the argument yet. This applies
to plain hookimpls as well as to wrappers and old-style hookwrappers.

.. versionchanged:: 1.7
    Previously a hookimpl's default value was always used, even when the hook
    call passed a value for the argument.
'''
assert anchor in s
s=s.replace(anchor,add,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
open('changelog/442.bugfix.rst','w').write("""A value passed by a hook call, or a hookspec's default value, now takes precedence over a default declared by a hookimpl for the same argument.
The hookimpl's own default is only used when neither the call nor the hookspec provides the argument.
""")
EOF

import pluggy

class S:
    @hs
    def h(self, a, b=5): pass
class P:
    @hi
    def h(self, a, b=1, c=7): return (a,b,c)
    @hi(wrapper=True)
    def h2(self): pass
class W:
    @hi(wrapper=True)
    def h(self, a, b=1):
        r = yield; return r+[("w",b)]
class O:
    @hi(hookwrapper=True)
    def h(self, b=1):
        yield; print("old", b)
pm=pluggy.PluginManager("x"); pm.add_hookspecs(S)
for p in (P(),W(),O()): pm.register(p) if not isinstance(p,P) else None
class P2:
    @hi
    def h(self, a, b=1, c=7): return (a,b,c)
pm.register(P2())
print(pm.hook.h(a=1, b=2)); print(pm.hook.h(a=1))
EOF
